The Bomb Gets a Disclaimer

Mohammad Javad Larijani has offered Iranian television a reassuring distinction. Nuclear weapons should spare civilians, he said, but military bases could be fair game for tactical use. The hypothetical mushroom cloud now comes with a targeting policy.

Larijani, a former deputy foreign minister who heads Iran’s Institute for Research in Fundamental Sciences, argued that the line between conventional and nuclear weapons matters less when the target is an enemy base. He also called for enriching uranium to 80% and said American bases in Germany, Albania, and Britain could become legitimate targets if used to attack Iran.

His remarks are part of a public push to reconsider Iran’s nuclear doctrine, which has not changed. Revolutionary Guards spokesman Hossein Mohebi said the force would prepare if the leadership ordered a change. A week earlier, security chief Mohsen Rezaei said the issue was under discussion but no official decision had been made.

Larijani is trying to make nuclear use sound acceptable by narrowing the address on the envelope. A military label on the target is a disclaimer. It does not explain how everyone outside the base would be spared.
